scope: Provider word events and measured durations for the film regressions. The closing scene uses the current course narrator. Earlier scenes retain their original measurements.

changed.previousSay: A useful policy can still make an unnecessary review. We chose its cut from the whole error bill and the available people. Keep authorization checks in force, then measure the frozen model and policy on fresh traffic. A score, an action, and an observed outcome each answer their own question.

renewal.timelineScope: Closing scene, with position reconstructed from provider durations and authored holds.

beats.say: The sigmoid maps a zero logit to one half, negative scores toward zero, and positive scores toward one. Follow the moving point. Around the center, shifting the score from minus one to one makes a large vertical change. The bracket measures that change.

Make the same two-unit move out in the tail, from four to six. The vertical change is much smaller. The curve is flattening. Our request's logit near one half maps to a score near point six two. The curve bounds the number; later outcomes must test its frequency meaning.

The logit is the logarithm of the positive-class odds. At a zero score the odds are one to one. Adding one to the logit multiplies the odds by e. Logistic regression assumes that these log odds are a linear combination of the evidence features.

Follow the chain rule backward. The loss derivative contains prediction minus label, divided by p times one minus p. The sigmoid contributes that same product. Those factors cancel, leaving prediction minus label. Each coefficient then receives this residual times its own feature.

Work one row. At zero weights, the probability is one half. This row needed review, so its residual is minus one half. Multiply by the intercept feature, ambiguity three point five, and support six. Subtracting these negative contributions raises the next score for similar cases.

One row gives a direction, but this update uses the whole batch. Every case starts at probability one half. Positive labels contribute a negative residual; routine labels contribute a positive one. The columns keep the intercept, ambiguity and support contributions separate.

Bring in all eight contributions, one request at a time. Keep each sign attached to its row while the column totals accumulate. Wait for the eighth row. Now divide the totals by eight to get the mean gradient.

Subtract the mean gradient, scaled by a learning rate of point two. The intercept stays zero, while both feature weights rise on this first step. That initial direction reflects the batch averages. Later steps can separate the two features' conditional effects.

Freeze the fitted weights. A threshold of one half asks for a logit of zero. That level is a straight line in our two-feature plane. The shaded side goes to review. Color inside each point still records its observed outcome.

Predict what a lower threshold will do. Move the line into the negative-score region. More requests acquire review rings, including some routine cases. The weights stay fixed. We have changed the action policy applied to the evidence score.

These eight earlier requests were reserved from fitting. Their closed outcomes are now available. Start with a high threshold. Route each request into its matching cell. A required review caught is a true positive; a required review passed through is a false negative.

Moving the threshold changes the queue and the errors together. Watch the crossed requests travel into their new cells. Their later labels stay attached. At the lower cut, all four required reviews are caught, along with two routine requests that add unnecessary queue work.

An unnecessary review costs eighteen dollars in this example. A missed required review costs a hundred and twenty. Calculate total cost at several thresholds. Multiply each kind of error by its own cost. More reviews have reduced this mistake bill, but we still have to staff the queue.

Return to the original scores. Group these reserved predictions into four bins. Each cyan bar is the group's average forecast. Leave the outcome covers on for a moment: the forecast existed before anyone could see how these requests ended.

Let their later labels arrive one at a time. Count required reviews inside each bin and divide by that bin's population. The lowest bin has one in three. Near our opening request's score, one of two needed review: a frequency of one half beside a forecast near point six one.

Two cases give a fragile fraction. Change just one label and half becomes all. More representative later labels must test the probability claim. If we fit a calibration map, reserve separate labels for verification, and reassess the numeric action cut on suitable validation data.

Back at our four-slot desk, the cut is one half. This request scores point six two four, so it goes to review. Open the closed case. Routine handling would have been enough. That makes this an unnecessary review. Put eighteen dollars on its bill.

Across the eight validation cases, one missed review cost a hundred and twenty dollars. One unnecessary review cost eighteen. That makes a hundred and thirty-eight dollars, with all four review slots filled. Freeze the cut and tally the next batch as its cases close. Next, we'll try a decision tree on a required review the straight line missed.
